issues: Nothing suggests an attempt to get around the measurement. The diff only changes the perturbation step of the basin-hopping loop: in half of the steps it now jitters the radii (scaled by U(0.6, 1.4), clipped to [0.01, 0.5]) instead of the centers. There is no file or network access, no hard-coded coordinates, and the RNG is the existing seeded one.
No bug makes the result meaningless. r0 is always set before _optimize is called, and _repair plus the existing validity checks still run on the output.
The candidate is worse than the incumbent: loss -2.6298 against -2.6360, so its sum of radii is about 0.0062 lower. Rejecting it is consistent with the numbers.

z cannot be recomputed from the numbers given. There is one run on each side, so there is no variance estimate. The reported |z| of 4400.69 implies a sigma of about 1.41e-6 (0.0062 / 4400.69), which matches the stated run-to-run noise floor of about 1e-6. That makes the size of z an artefact of the assumed noise, not a measured spread. The sign and the reject decision still hold.
Minor: the incumbent's 2.6360 is slightly above the rounded 'best known 2.635' on the program card. This is within rounding of the known value (about 2.6359), so it is not an integrity concern.
